title: Build and integrate backend services and data pipelines
description: Develop service-side software using Python or Java and connect it to APIs and REST endpoints. Apply Linux or Ubuntu environments, Kafka, Spark, and Redis to support data movement, processing, and caching in a service architecture.
soft_skills_description: Work with clear requirements, coordinate interface contracts with other developers, and troubleshoot service behavior systematically.
rationale: The listed skills cluster around backend engineering rather than general programming because they combine implementation languages with service protocols and infrastructure tools. Python, Java, API, and REST show the ability to build and consume services, while Linux, Ubuntu, Kafka, Spark, and Redis indicate deployment and data-flow support. A learner can prove mastery by implementing a working service, integrating an API, and using a cache or message stream appropriately. This outcome is distinct from the UI competency because it focuses on server-side logic and from the observability/security competency because it emphasizes functional delivery over operational monitoring.
future_relevance: Stable: backend integration, streaming, and caching remain core building blocks in software systems across industries.

title: Build SQL and Power BI analytics for business reporting
description: Use SQL, Power BI, and analytics methods to prepare, analyze, and present data for operational or business reporting. Apply optimization and technical problem-solving to improve query performance and dashboard usefulness.
soft_skills_description: Learners must interpret data correctly, check results carefully, and explain findings in a way that supports decisions.
rationale: SQL, Power BI, analytics, and optimization form a coherent data-reporting competency that appears repeatedly in the cluster. Accounting is included because it provides the business context often used for reports and dashboards, especially in operational settings. Learners can demonstrate mastery by writing queries, building a dashboard, and explaining the reported metrics to users. This competency is distinct from requirements analysis because its output is data products and insights rather than problem definition.
future_relevance: Stable; SQL and BI reporting continue to be core skills even as analytics platforms evolve.

title: Develop cross-platform web and mobile user interfaces
description: Create user interfaces with React for web applications and build or adapt mobile solutions for Android and iOS. Connect the interface to platform services so users can interact with application features consistently across devices.
soft_skills_description: Translate requirements into usable screens, adjust designs for different device constraints, and explain interface choices to stakeholders.
rationale: React, Android, iOS, and platform form a coherent application-delivery theme centered on user-facing software across devices. These skills differ from backend engineering because the main task is presenting features, handling interaction, and ensuring the interface works on target platforms. A learner can demonstrate mastery by producing a responsive web app and a mobile prototype that uses shared data or services. AI platforms is kept here only as an application environment cue, but not as the core focus; the competency remains about building usable interfaces, which is distinct from security and operations work.
future_relevance: Stable: organizations continue to need web and mobile interfaces, even as device ecosystems and frameworks evolve.

title: Use Azure and AWS cloud infrastructure to support application deployment
description: Set up and use core cloud infrastructure and cloud services on Azure and AWS for application hosting. Configure basic resources, understand the role of cloud platforms, and choose appropriate cloud services for a given deployment scenario.
soft_skills_description: Learners must record configuration choices clearly and troubleshoot basic deployment issues using systematic steps.
rationale: The listed skills all point to foundational cloud-platform knowledge, with Azure and AWS as the main named environments and cloud infrastructure/services as the common capability. The competency is phrased as an action because learners should be able to provision, explain, and use basic cloud resources in a controlled environment. Mastery can be shown by deploying an application component and identifying why a cloud service was selected. It is distinct from the Azure DevOps competency because it focuses on the hosting platform rather than the delivery pipeline.
future_relevance: Stable: Azure and AWS remain dominant cloud platforms, and foundational cloud infrastructure skills continue to be widely used in software roles.

title: Support modern application infrastructure and deployment practices
description: Work with infrastructure, PaaS, and CI/CD to deploy and support software in controlled environments. Follow standard design-system and system-setup practices to keep services reliable and maintainable.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to follow deployment steps accurately, diagnose basic environment issues, and coordinate with peers when releases fail.
rationale: The infrastructure, PaaS, and CI/CD items clearly indicate a deployment and operations-oriented competency. Design system is retained because it suggests standardized platform or interface patterns that support consistent delivery, even if it is less central than the other items. A learner could show mastery by deploying a sample app through a pipeline and explaining the environment components involved. It is distinct from the reporting competency because the main concern is hosting, release, and reliability rather than analytics output.
future_relevance: Emerging; CI/CD and PaaS usage continue to expand as teams automate delivery and cloud deployment.

title: Develop and document technical solutions and workflows
description: Create tools, technical documentation, and supporting workflows that help teams deliver and maintain software systems. Coordinate small projects, maintain records, and solve technical problems according to agreed procedures.
soft_skills_description: Learners should manage files and task status carefully, write precise documentation, and coordinate with teammates during delivery.
rationale: These skills cluster around implementation support and the disciplined communication needed to sustain software work. Confluence and documentation tasks indicate that writing, maintaining, and sharing technical knowledge is part of the role, while develop tools and solve technical problems show practical delivery. Learners can prove mastery by producing a small utility, documenting setup and usage, and keeping project notes current. It is separate from requirements analysis because it starts after needs are defined and focuses on building, recording, and coordinating execution.
future_relevance: Stable; documentation and workflow support remain critical for maintainable software teams.

title: Apply machine learning methods to analyze data
description: Use machine learning and data analysis techniques to prepare data, choose an appropriate model approach, and interpret results. Validate model performance and explain the basic factors that affect accuracy and generalization.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to interpret patterns in data, compare model outputs, and decide whether results are acceptable for the task.
rationale: The title captures the cluster's strongest recurring theme: machine learning supported by data analysis. These skills naturally belong together because learners must analyze data before selecting and testing a model. Mastery can be shown by preparing a dataset, applying a standard ML method, and explaining evaluation results. It is distinct from the other competencies because it focuses on foundational model-building rather than generative content creation or domain-specific AI applications.
future_relevance: Stable: machine learning remains a core capability across software and data-driven systems.

title: Automate software workflows using AI-enabled tools
description: Design and implement automated workflows that reduce manual steps in software development or operations. Use AI-enabled workflows and automation to improve repeatability, consistency, and task completion speed. Learners should be able to document the workflow, implement the automation, and test that it performs as intended.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to follow workflow requirements carefully, notice failure points, and adjust automations based on observed behavior.
rationale: The title matches the cluster’s strongest repeated theme: using automation and AI-enabled workflows to streamline repetitive work. The description is practical and assessable because learners can show a working workflow, test results, and basic documentation. It is distinct from architecture-focused competencies because it emphasizes process improvement and task automation rather than system structure. The included skills are tightly aligned and reinforce one another without forcing unrelated concepts into the outcome.
future_relevance: Emerging, because AI-assisted automation is expanding quickly across software development, operations, and business workflows.

title: Manage containerized application delivery with Docker, Kubernetes, and DevOps practices
description: Build and run applications in Docker containers, then deploy and manage them in Kubernetes environments. Apply DevOps practices to support reliable builds, releases, monitoring, and collaboration across development and operations.
soft_skills_description: Learners should be able to coordinate build and release tasks with others, diagnose basic deployment issues, and communicate operational status clearly.
rationale: Docker, Kubernetes, and DevOps are strongly related because they describe the packaging, orchestration, and operating model used to deliver software reliably. Docker covers container creation, Kubernetes covers deployment and scaling, and DevOps provides the workflow mindset that connects development with operations. Mastery can be demonstrated by containerizing an application, deploying it to Kubernetes, and supporting a basic release flow with operational checks. This competency is separate from infrastructure provisioning because it focuses on application runtime and delivery rather than creating the underlying cloud environment.
future_relevance: Stable: container-based delivery and DevOps practices are widely adopted and continue to underpin scalable software operations.

title: Manage commerce operations across retail, inventory, supply chain, and logistics workflows
description: Coordinate operational tasks in retail and commerce settings by tracking inventory, understanding supply chain flow, and supporting logistics activities. Use standard procedures to keep products moving from stock to customer delivery.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to work with others to keep operations accurate and respond to routine stock or delivery issues.
rationale: Commerce, retail, inventory management, supply chain, and logistics belong together because they describe one end-to-end operational chain. The repeated commerce and retail terms reinforce that the cluster points to business operations rather than a narrow software feature. A learner can show competence by updating stock information, following fulfillment steps, and explaining how goods move through the chain. This is distinct from the finance competency because it centers on product flow and operational coordination, not accounting or planning.
future_relevance: Stable, because retail and fulfillment operations continue to depend on structured inventory and logistics processes even as platforms become more digital.

title: Monitor systems and support secure operational workflows
description: Use observability tools to track application behavior, identify incidents, and support resolution through workflow systems such as ServiceNow and Jira. Apply cybersecurity awareness when handling incidents, platform issues, and operational follow-up.
soft_skills_description: Record incidents clearly, escalate issues appropriately, and coordinate with peers to restore service safely and quickly.
rationale: Observability, ServiceNow, and Jira point to a practical operations competency focused on monitoring, incident handling, and work tracking. Cybersecurity is included because operational support now routinely requires secure handling of alerts, access, and remediation steps. A learner can demonstrate mastery by interpreting logs or metrics, raising and tracking incidents, and documenting resolution actions in a ticketing workflow. This competency is separate from software construction competencies because it emphasizes reliability, response, and secure process rather than code or interface implementation.
future_relevance: Emerging: observability and security operations are becoming more important as systems grow more distributed and regulated.

title: Gather and analyze business requirements for software solutions
description: Elicit, clarify, and document user and stakeholder requirements for software or reporting solutions. Analyze existing systems and business processes to translate needs into actionable specifications and implementation priorities.
soft_skills_description: Learners need to communicate with non-technical stakeholders, listen for hidden needs, and negotiate priorities when requirements conflict.
rationale: The listed skills consistently point to requirement discovery and analysis rather than coding alone. Using both Business Analysis labels and the actions gather/understand requirements and analyze systems keeps the competency grounded in real job tasks. A learner could demonstrate mastery by interviewing stakeholders, producing clear requirement notes, and mapping needs into functional specifications. It is distinct from documentation or BI delivery because the focus is on understanding and structuring the problem before building.
future_relevance: Stable; requirements analysis remains essential as teams adopt more automation and self-service tools.
